headline.purpose: View title and donut centre figure; 20px / 17px on phones.

body.purpose: Default text, Category names, controls, nav items and amounts.

body-sm.purpose: Card meta, comparisons, shares, Subcategory rows, captions.

label.purpose: Nav group headings, table headers, count badge, Account pill. Sentence case.

wordmark.purpose: "Purse" in ink at 700, "graph" in Indigo Ink at 600, beside the mark.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Every card; the pressed theme-switch segment.

shadows.name: card-dark
shadows.purpose: Card lift in dark: deeper shadow plus a 3% white hairline ring.

shadows.name: control
shadows.purpose: Buttons, selects and the period stepper.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Every focusable element; 6px radius on the ring.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Chevron rotation (.2s) and the phone More and Filter sheets' slide up (.25s). HTMX swaps themselves are instant.

motion.name: donut-sweep
motion.purpose: The donut's single entrance; off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No movement, state kept: charts render final, chevron flips, sheets appear (at most a 120ms opacity fade), loading line static at 50%, the loading dim still applies. Scrolling is always instant.

themes.chartRetheme: theme.js dispatches a themechange event on document (also on prefers-color-scheme change while System is active); dashboard.js rebuilds ECharts options from getComputedStyle custom properties and calls setOption(..., { notMerge: true }), also on resize. ECharts 5.6 has no live setTheme.
themes.noFlash: Blocking inline script in base.html <head>, before the stylesheet, applies localStorage 'theme' (light|dark|system, else system) to data-theme before first paint; <html> ships data-theme="system".

dataColour.awaiting: awaiting grey plus 45deg hatch; donut decal rgba(255,255,255,.45)
dataColour.incomeSubcategories: the Income Category's hue (Money in bars, Sankey income nodes)
dataColour.moneyOut: muted (a neutral; spending as a whole is no Category)
dataColour.awaitingLine: dashed awaiting grey (a line can't carry the hatch)

charts.style: Classic axes (#64, variant A): legend top-left, quiet axes, axis tooltips as tables, a table beside every chart
charts.legend: top-left, 8px circle icons, ink-2 Inter 500 12px, 16px gap, scrolls; inactive line-strong
charts.valueAxis: whole euros (Intl sl-SI EUR, maximumFractionDigits 0), muted 12px; solid line gridlines; no axis line or ticks
charts.categoryAxis: line-strong baseline, no ticks, muted 12px labels
charts.tooltip: card fill, line border, 10px radius, pop shadow, ink 13px; axis tooltip = table sorted biggest first with a Total row; cents in amounts; Net signed
charts.emphasis: focus series; blur lines to .15, bar segments to .25
charts.cashflow: grouped bars: Money in = Income hue, Money out = muted, max 22px, 4px top radius; Net = 2px ink line, 7px points ringed in card
charts.trends: 2px lines in Category hue, points on hover only; Awaiting review dashed
charts.perMember: horizontal stacked bars per Bucket, max 28px, 1.5px card-coloured segment borders, Awaiting hatched
charts.sankey: nodes 12px wide, 2px radius, 10px gap; links gradient at .3 (.6 on hover, adjacency focus); income labels left, Household top, the rest right, 'name amount'; overlapping labels hidden; Household ink-2, Saved/From savings/others muted

completeness.source: Coverage, derived and read-only; only the Accounts the filters include; Accounts with no Statements never count
completeness.monthStates: Complete | Partial (a Gap in it) | Partly tracked (before some included Account's first Coverage day, not all) | In progress (running month, no Gap) | Not tracked (before every included Account's first Coverage day)
completeness.periodState: first of Partial, Partly tracked, In progress, Not tracked, Complete among its months; wholly Not tracked = empty state
completeness.headerLine: between view bar and stat tiles; ink-2 13px, muted 16px info icon, no fill/border/alert colour; 'Incomplete: no Statements yet from <Account> for <range>' (Accounts link to Import, >2 collapse to 'and N more') · '<Account> is tracked from <date>' (no link) · '<amount> (<share>) still awaiting review' (links to Review queue); absent when neither applies
completeness.monthAxisBands: Partial / Partly tracked / In progress: full-height band in hover (a bar series on hidden axes; Trends uses boundaryGap true), muted 11px top label 'Partial' / 'Partly tracked' / 'So far'; running month axis label 'Oct (so far)'; tooltip opens with the reason
completeness.notTracked: month keeps its axis slot, faint label, data null (no bar; lines break); tooltip 'No Statements yet'
completeness.tables: headers 'Jul (partial)' / 'Jan (partly tracked)' / 'Oct (so far)'; '—' in Not tracked cells, never 0
completeness.statTiles: comparison becomes 'Not comparable: <Month> is incomplete' when either side isn't Complete
completeness.stepper: previous disabled at the period holding the Household's first Coverage day (filter-independent); typed earlier URLs still render, as Not tracked
completeness.defaults: last full month for every view; Category trends = 12 months ending with it; running month only via next
completeness.reserved: no hatch or dash: those mean Awaiting review

components.name: Button

components.html: <button class="ds-btn" type="button"><svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M3 10h18L12 4zM5 10v8M9.5 10v8M14.5 10v8M19 10v8M3 20h18"/></svg>All Accounts<svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="m6 9 6 6 6-6"/></svg></button>

components.css: .ds-cats { width: 560px; font: 14px/1.5 Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; color: var(--ink, #111827); } .ds-cat { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) 140px 52px 104px; align-items: center; gap: 12px; width: 100%; padding: 10px 12px; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; background: none; font: inherit; color: inherit; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-cat:hover { background: var(--hover, #f3f4f6); } .ds-cat.open { background: var(--accent-soft, #eef2ff); } .ds-cat:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus, #6366f1); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-name { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; display: inline-block; } .ds-bar { height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--ground, #f4f5f7); overflow: hidden; } .ds-bar i { display: block; height: 100%; border-radius: inherit; } .ds-share { color: var(--muted, #6b7280); font-size: 13px; text-align: right; } .ds-amt { font-weight: 600; text-align: right; } .ds-awaiting .ds-dot { background: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, var(--awaiting, #9ca3af) 0 2px, transparent 2px 4px); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--awaiting, #9ca3af); } .ds-awaiting .ds-bar i { background: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, var(--awaiting, #9ca3af) 0 3px, color-mix(in srgb, var(--awaiting, #9ca3af) 40%, transparent) 3px 6px); }

narrative.overview:
Pursegraph deliberately looks like a polished personal-finance dashboard: a light sidebar, white cards on a cool grey ground, stat tiles, a Category donut and a single indigo accent. Monarch Money's craft is the bar. The convention is the point, because familiarity serves the least technical Member reading the Dashboard on a phone. Nothing quirky is smuggled in. Distinction comes from execution: exact figures, steady Category hues, quiet type and soft lift.

The density is calm, not terminal-like. A view shows a few large figures, one chart and one ranked list, and detail opens on request (drill-down) rather than up front. Copy and colour describe and never judge. A comparison reads "523,55 € less than September" in muted grey, with no red or green verdict. Dark mode is the same world at night: a near-black ground, raised graphite cards, and the same Category hues lifted in lightness so they keep their identity.

The real app is server-rendered Django templates with HTMX, hand-written CSS custom properties and no build step. ECharts draws the charts. Every asset is self-hosted, including Inter as an OFL variable woff2 under `static/fonts/`, because the app runs offline from the internet on the LAN or a VPN.
keyCharacteristics: Cool grey ground, white 14px cards with soft ambient shadow, one indigo accent used only for chrome.
Inter throughout, with tabular figures on every amount, and sl-SI number formatting ("1.234,56 €").
Ten Category hues (Tableau-10-derived), keyed by Category id and identical in every view, with a lifted set for dark.
Charts that never rely on colour alone: directly labelled donut segments, and a hatch for Awaiting review.
1.5px stroke icons, sentence-case labels, no uppercase tracking.
Light, System and Dark themes, with the system as the default.

rules.name: The One Indigo Rule
rules.body: Indigo belongs to the interface: active state, count badge, links, focus, the wordmark and the mark. It is never a data colour, never a chart series and never a Category.

rules.name: The Fixed Hue Rule
rules.body: A Category wears the same hue in every view, chart and theme step (lifted in dark, never re-assigned). Hues are keyed by Category id, never by sort order.

rules.name: The Neutral Wait Rule
rules.body: Awaiting review is neutral grey plus a 45° hatch, everywhere it appears (dot, bar and donut segment). It never borrows a Category hue.

rules.name: The No Verdict Rule
rules.body: No red/green good/bad colouring. Comparisons are muted text that describes the difference, and Net is plain ink with its sign. A Category hue that happens to be red or green (cat-8, cat-1) carries no meaning beyond its Category.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every amount, share, count and date figure uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Locale Figure Rule
rules.body: Amounts format with `Intl.NumberFormat('sl-SI', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR', useGrouping: 'always' })`, giving "1.234,56 €". Shares are whole percent with a space ("26 %"). Net carries an explicit sign.

rules.name: The Soft Lift Rule
rules.body: Depth is diffuse and ambient, never a hard offset. Cards are borderless in light. Hairlines divide content inside cards, not cards from the ground.

dos: **Do** key every Category's hue to its Category id (`cat-((id − 1) mod 10)`), and use the same hue in every view and chart.
**Do** label donut segments directly and hatch Awaiting review, so no chart relies on colour alone.
**Do** set every figure in tabular numerals and format amounts as sl-SI EUR with grouping always on ("1.234,56 €").
**Do** write comparisons as neutral muted sentences ("523,55 € less than September").

**Do** define every colour as a CSS custom property, with a `[data-theme="dark"]` block and a `prefers-color-scheme` block for `data-theme="system"`, and rebuild chart options from those properties when the theme changes.
**Do** self-host every asset, including Inter (variable woff2 under `static/fonts/`) and ECharts.
**Do** turn motion off under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The donut sweep, chevron rotation and drawer slide (cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)) are the whole motion vocabulary.
donts: **Don't** use the indigo accent as a data colour, a chart series or a Category hue.
**Don't** give Awaiting review a Category hue, or show it without its hatch.
**Don't** colour spending, Net or comparisons red or green to mean good or bad.
**Don't** add uppercase tracked labels, kickers or eyebrows above titles. Labels are sentence case.
**Don't** use hard offset shadows or borders around cards. Lift is soft and ambient.
**Don't** load fonts, scripts or styles from a CDN in production.
